# quilt-lab

The fleet's experiment protocol as a tool: **register → run → receipt → seal**.
Tools that make tools.

Zero dependencies. Node ≥ 18. One CLI (`lab.mjs`), one worked example, one
hash-chained ledger. Every later experiment gets the same verbs, the same
evidence shape, and the same failure semantics — which is what makes
experiments cheap to run, cheap to reproduce, and cheap to trust.

## Lineage

- **wave-66, [quilt-neighbourhood](https://github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-neighbourhood)** — content-addressed CellDiff DAG with a registered policy and a receipt chain; 8/8 tests including forgery rejection and chain-tamper detection.
- **wave-66, [slackwater-quilt](https://github.com/SuperInstance/slackwater-quilt)** — "the ledger is the build": replayed receipt chain as build state, with ghost-receipt adjudication; 12/12 tests.
- Both PoCs proved receipt discipline **ad hoc**. quilt-lab standardizes it: the discipline stops being a per-repo achievement and becomes a tool any lane can pick up in five minutes (see [TEMPLATE.md](TEMPLATE.md)).

## Quickstart (the worked example is committed)

```sh
node lab.mjs run linear-cell-regression     # deterministic GD on seeded synthetic data
node lab.mjs run linear-cell-regression     # again — metrics.json bytes are identical
node lab.mjs receipt linear-cell-regression # RECEIPT.md: what ran / what returned / what counts as failure
node lab.mjs seal linear-cell-regression    # hash-chain the evidence into LEDGER.jsonl
node lab.mjs verify                         # walk the chain, detect tampering
```

`experiments/linear-cell-regression/` is the reference implementation of the
protocol: seeded synthetic data (`y = 2x + 1 + uniform noise`, seed 42),
full-batch gradient descent, 500 steps, metrics
`{mse_final, mse_trajectory_sha, steps}` — byte-identical on every run.

## Commands

| command                | what it does                                                                                              | exit 1 when                                  |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `register <spec.json>` | validate spec, pin its canonical sha256 in `experiments/REGISTRY.md`                                       | malformed spec, taken name w/ different spec |
| `run <name>`           | execute `run(ctx)`, write `runs/<run_id>/{metrics.json,meta.json,log.txt}`                                 | budget exceeded, error, failure condition    |
| `receipt <name>`       | write `experiments/<name>/RECEIPT.md` from the latest run (three elements + metrics sha256)                | no completed run, unregistered name          |
| `seal <name>`          | append `{name, run_id, metrics_sha, prev_seal, seal}` to `LEDGER.jsonl`                                    | unregistered, no run, already sealed         |
| `verify`               | recompute every seal, check linkage + duplicates + sealed-evidence hashes                                   | **any** tampering                            |
| `help`                 | usage + doctrine (short form)                                                                              | —                                            |

`--root <dir>` (or env `QUILTLAB_ROOT`) points the CLI at any workspace — the
test suite uses this to stay hermetic.

## Guarantees

1. **Determinism you can check**: same seed ⇒ byte-identical `metrics.json`.
   Everything non-deterministic (run_id, wall time, status) lives in
   `meta.json`, outside the sealed evidence.
2. **Registration pins intent**: specs are hashed canonically; `run` refuses
   spec drift; a taken name refuses a different spec.
3. **Receipts are complete or they don't exist**: three elements — what ran /
   what returned (exact numbers) / what counts as failure — plus the sha256 of
   the exact metrics bytes.
4. **Nothing is done until sealed**: the ledger is an append-only hash chain;
   each seal commits to the metrics digest and the previous tip.
5. **Tampering is loud**: flip one byte in the ledger or in sealed evidence and
   `lab verify` names the line and the mismatch (tested: NC1, NC1b).

## Layout

```
lab.mjs                                  the whole harness (zero dependencies)
experiments/REGISTRY.md                  registered specs, pinned by sha256
experiments/linear-cell-regression/      the worked example (spec + index + README)
experiments/<name>/runs/<run_id>/        per-run evidence (metrics/meta/log) — gitignored
experiments/<name>/RECEIPT.md            three-element receipt for the latest run
LEDGER.jsonl                             append-only seal chain (genesis = 64 zeros)
TEMPLATE.md                              add an experiment in 5 minutes
test/harness.test.mjs                    T1–T5 + NC1/NC1b/NC2
TEST-RECEIPT.md                          the suite's own receipt (actual numbers)
```

## Testing & CI

```sh
node --test test/*.test.mjs
```

- **T1** register idempotence (identical spec = no-op; different spec under a taken name refused)
- **T2** run determinism (two runs → byte-identical metrics)
- **T3** receipt contains the three elements + correct sha256
- **T4** seal chain verifies (genesis link, N+1 link, double-seal refusal)
- **T5** the real worked example runs byte-identically twice
- **NC1** one flipped byte in `LEDGER.jsonl` → verify false
- **NC1b** one flipped byte in sealed `metrics.json` → verify false
- **NC2** unknown experiment name fails loudly (run/receipt/seal)

CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) runs the suite on Node 20 and 24 and then
verifies the shipped ledger chain.

## Limitations (honest)

- Single-process, single-machine: no distributed locking on `LEDGER.jsonl` —
  seal from one lane at a time (sequential CLI use, as designed).
- The wall-clock budget is a race, not a kill: a non-cooperative experiment
  that ignores its promise is abandoned at the cap and the process exits hard
  (`process.exit`), but its pending work dies with the process, unrecorded.
- The hash chain is tamper-*evident*, not tamper-*proof*: sha256 is public, so
  a wholesale chain rewrite is only caught because the **tip** is anchored
  externally (TEST-RECEIPT.md, release notes). Anchor every tip you publish.
- Fresh clones verify chain integrity but not sealed evidence (runs/ are
  gitignored) — receipts carry the exact numbers, so the receipt is the
  human-readable anchor.
